prompt:
Output exactly one concise, information‑dense caption: a single grammatical sentence, composed of comma‑separated short phrases, describing only visibly present facts. Use digits for counts, no inference, hedging, or metaphors (no "appears/likely/seems"); do not output anything else.

Required ordering for the sentence (include each item only if clearly visible; omit unverifiable items). Prefer ≤30 words:
1) Begin with digit(s) + subject noun(s) + spatial anchor for each counted subject: [left|center|right] and [foreground|midground|background]. If partly out of frame, use "partially cropped at [edge]".
2) Immediately after, include one visible action if present plus the specific body/vehicle part or object involved (e.g., "right hand on fretboard", "left foot stepping", "holding knife at table edge"). Run the micro‑action checklist before using "no-action-visible"; use "no-action-visible" only if absolutely no limb/object contact, gaze direction, posture, object displacement, or interaction is detectable.
3) Add 1–3 high‑signal discriminative descriptor(s), chosen by priority: (A) exact legible text (transcribe in quotes and localize, e.g., "'NO PARKING' stenciled on roll‑up door at background right") > (B) reflection/wetness/surface condition > (C) material/texture > (D) distinctive accessory (hat, bag) > (E) color. If >3 candidates exist, select top 3 by this priority.
4) If a person/object interacts with another object/structure, require one part‑level relation phrase (e.g., "sitting on metal chair beside small round table", "rear wheel off ground").
5) Optionally include exactly one viewpoint token when obvious: {close-up, medium, wide, high-angle, low-angle}. Omit if unclear.
6) Optionally include exactly one lighting token when obvious: {backlit, front-lit, rim-lit, long-shadow-left, long-shadow-right}. Omit if unclear.
7) If visible, add one concise background landmark/texture noun phrase (single phrase, e.g., "wet pavement with ripples", "stone embankment", "storefront window", "pier with canopy").
8) Preserve the final ordering in the sentence: [digit+subject+location], [action+part if any], [1–3 descriptors], [viewpoint if included], [lighting if included], [background phrase].

Pre-output verification checklist (must be applied before emitting the caption):
- Did I detect any legible text? If yes, transcribe exact string in quotes and localize.
- Did I detect limb/object contact, gaze, posture, object displacement, or interaction? If yes, include action+part phrase; otherwise use "no-action-visible" or omit action.
- Did I spot reflections, wet surfaces, or distinctive background landmarks? If yes, include one background noun phrase.
- Are small props or distinctive clothing/accessories visible? If yes, include up to the top descriptor(s) per priority.
- Is any subject partially out of frame? If yes, use "partially cropped at [edge]".

Style and constraints:
- Use compact, active, factual phrasing and concrete nouns (prefer canonical object names: "acoustic guitar" not "instrument" when specific). Limit descriptors to the top 3 priority items.
- Do not infer ages, emotions, relationships, or unverified attributes. No hedging words.
- Keep punctuation simple and phrases comma‑separated in one sentence.

Micro‑examples (do not output these; follow their style):
Positive: "1 man center foreground, right hand on fretboard, reddish‑brown acoustic guitar body, medium, front-lit, wet pavement with reflections." 
Positive: "2 boats center and left foreground, people boarding at stern, white hulls with red trim, wide, front-lit, stone embankment behind."
Negative (avoid): "Several people in a busy scene with objects and unclear lighting."
